key_insight: Directly optimizing pass@k selects partial reasoning paths to maximize the chance of at least one correct completion, naturally balancing quality and diversity.
engineering_relevance: Pruning candidate solutions after short prefixes can reduce inference computation while preserving promising, nonredundant reasoning paths.
method: Generate short prefixes for a pool of candidate solutions.
Select a subset by optimizing its probability of producing at least one correct answer.
Continue only the selected candidates to completion.
evidence_signal: Across eight open-weight reasoning models, the method outperforms quality-based and diversity-based pruning baselines, with especially pronounced gains when retaining a moderate number of candidates.
watch_item: The abstract does not specify how the pass@k objective is estimated or the computational overhead of optimizing it.
paper_title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
